course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions

quiz.title: Unit 2 FRQ 2: Modeling a non-periodic context (Topics 2.1 to 2.8)
quiz.headline: Build an exponential model from two data points, use average rates of change, and explain a limitation of the model.
quiz.promptTitle: Free response 2 · Modeling a non-periodic context · graphing calculator
quiz.prompt: A study app launched in a school district. The number of students using the app t months after launch is modeled by U(t) = abᵗ, where a and b are positive constants. One month after launch, 1200 students were using the app, and three months after launch, 2700 students were using the app.
quiz.instructions: Part A style: a graphing calculator is required. Show the work that leads to each answer; answers without supporting work may not earn credit where work is requested. Avoid rounding intermediate values, and give decimal approximations accurate to three places after the decimal point unless the part says otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, the domain of a function f is the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number.
quiz.note: Original practice question written in the AP Precalculus free-response format (6 points, parts A to C). Scoring is self-assessed with the point-by-point rubric. It is not an official AP question or an official AP score.

scaffold.label: Show work
scaffold.text: Write the setup, such as the expression you evaluate or the equation you solve, before the answer.

scaffold.label: Use notation
scaffold.text: Use limit notation, interval notation, and units exactly where a part asks for them.

scaffold.label: Justify
scaffold.text: When a part says give a reason or explain, refer to the given values or the context.

responseFields.label: Part A (i)
responseFields.prompt: A (i). Use the given data to write two equations that can be used to find the values for constants a and b in the expression for U(t).
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part A (ii)
responseFields.prompt: A (ii). Find the values for a and b as decimal approximations.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (i)
responseFields.prompt: B (i). Use the given data to find the average rate of change of the number of students using the app, in students per month, from t = 1 to t = 3 months. Show the computations that lead to your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (ii)
responseFields.prompt: B (ii). Using the model, compare the average rates of change of U over the intervals 1 ≤ t ≤ 2 and 2 ≤ t ≤ 3. Is the number of students increasing at an increasing rate or at a decreasing rate? Give a reason for your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (i)
responseFields.prompt: C (i). Use the model to find the value of t, in months, at which 10,000 students are using the app. Express your answer as a decimal approximation.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (ii)
responseFields.prompt: C (ii). The school district has 15,000 students. Explain why the model U is not appropriate for predicting the number of users 12 months after launch. Refer to the model and to the context in your explanation.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

rubric.label: A (i) Two equations
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for ab = 1200 and ab³ = 2700.

rubric.label: A (ii) Values of a and b
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for b = 1.5 and a = 800 (b² = 2700/1200 = 2.25).

rubric.label: B (i) Average rate of change
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for (2700 − 1200)/(3 − 1) = 750 students per month, with the computation shown.

rubric.label: B (ii) Increasing at an increasing rate, with reason
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: U(2) = 1800, so the average rates of change are 600 students per month on [1, 2] and 900 students per month on [2, 3]; they are positive and increasing, so the number of students is increasing at an increasing rate.

rubric.label: C (i) Value of t
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for 800(1.5)ᵗ = 10000 with t = 6.229 months.

rubric.label: C (ii) Limitation
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for explaining that U(12) = 800(1.5)¹² ≈ 103,797, which is far more than the 15,000 students in the district, because an exponential model increases without bound while the number of users cannot exceed 15,000.

quiz.modelResponse:
A (i). U(1) = 1200 and U(3) = 2700 give ab = 1200 and ab³ = 2700.

A (ii). Dividing, ab³/(ab) = b² = 2700/1200 = 2.25, so b = 1.5 (b > 0). Then a = 1200/1.5 = 800. U(t) = 800(1.5)ᵗ.

B (i). (U(3) − U(1))/(3 − 1) = (2700 − 1200)/2 = 750. The average rate of change is 750 students per month.

B (ii). U(2) = 800(1.5)² = 1800. Over [1, 2] the average rate of change is (1800 − 1200)/1 = 600 students per month, and over [2, 3] it is (2700 − 1800)/1 = 900 students per month. Both are positive and the second is greater, so the number of students is increasing at an increasing rate.

C (i). 800(1.5)ᵗ = 10000, so (1.5)ᵗ = 12.5. Using a graphing calculator, t = 6.229 months.

C (ii). The model gives U(12) = 800(1.5)¹² ≈ 103,797 students. An exponential model with b > 1 increases without bound, but the number of users cannot be more than the 15,000 students in the district. So U is not appropriate for t = 12.
quiz.alternateModel: In A (ii) a graphing calculator may be used to solve the system. In C (ii) it is also correct to find when the model reaches 15,000, at t ≈ 7.229 months, and explain that predictions after that time exceed the district's population.
commonErrors: Writing a + b = 1200, a linear relationship, instead of ab = 1200.
Using b² = 2.25 as the value of b.
Reporting 1500 students, the change, instead of dividing by 2 months.
Saying 'increasing' without comparing two average rates of change.
Saying the model fails 'because it is a model' without referring to the 15,000-student limit.
